transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We're here for the weekly enforcement review on the Northstar Systems royalty matter. As you know, their quarterly reports show inconsistent usage figures, and the commercial team wants this handled without disrupting the existing license. Before I can approve any enforcement plan, I need to hear concrete recommendations from each of our four specialists — finance, IP, privacy, and account counsel. I'll record each recommendation in the enforcement checklist, and once all four have been stated, I'll make my final call. I also need the final plan to identify whether we're issuing a formal audit notice or a general breach letter, along with a specific implementation commitment for whichever notice we choose. Let's get started — who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. I'd be happy to go first on the finance side. I've completed a reconciliation of Northstar's usage ledger against their royalty reports, and I can confirm there is a quantified underpayment for the third and fourth quarters of 2025. However, I should note that the reconciliation is still awaiting controller sign-off and has not yet been entered in the legal enforcement dashboard, so the figure is not yet officially logged. Given that we have a confirmed discrepancy and the license agreement expressly permits a royalty audit when reporting discrepancies are identified, my finance recommendation is that we proceed with a formal audit notice rather than a general breach letter. The audit right is contractually available to us, and a formal audit notice is the more precise instrument for addressing a quantified usage-and-royalty discrepancy. As for implementation commitment, I recommend that the formal audit notice be issued within five business days of controller sign-off on the reconciliation, with the audit scope expressly limited to Q3 and Q4 2025 usage and royalty reporting.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we finalize the notice type and implementation plan, I need to share what I found in my review of the license agreement. I completed a clause review yesterday and confirmed that an audit notice under this agreement must be sent at least 10 business days before the audit, must identify the auditor as Grant & Pike LLP, and may not be replaced by a general breach letter. I had not yet circulated these notice requirements, so I want everyone to have them now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share what I've confirmed on the privacy side. I reached out to Northstar's privacy lead and confirmed that the audit materials will include EU employee-level usage records. The approved method is an on-site review using pseudonymized records, with no export of EU employee data — rather than a remote transfer of the raw files. This is critical for our audit notice and implementation plan: the audit must be structured as an on-site review with pseudonymized records, and we cannot request remote transfer of raw EU employee data. My privacy recommendation is that we proceed with a formal audit notice, with the implementation commitment that the audit be conducted on-site at Northstar's premises using pseudonymized EU employee usage records, with no export or remote transfer of EU employee data, and that the notice explicitly reference this on-site pseudonymized approach.

transcript.text: Before we finalize the audit notice and implementation plan, I need to share what I learned during this week's executive-account call. Northstar will accept a private cure process only if it receives 30 days to cure after the demand and the company makes no public accusation. This commercial condition has not yet been added to the enforcement draft, and it directly affects how we structure the notice and implementation timeline.
